content.title: Navigation With Links
content.hook: A routed application needs navigation that behaves like navigation.
content.context:
Next.js provides the `Link` component for internal navigation.

```tsx
import Link from 'next/link';

<Link href="/dashboard">Dashboard</Link>
```
goals: Master Navigation With Links: This UI represents navigation to another route.

content.question:
What route does this link target?

```tsx
<Link href="/settings">Settings</Link>
```

content.title: Why not ordinary strings?
content.text:
A route is more than text on a screen.

The application needs to interpret navigation as a meaningful action.

A dedicated navigation component gives the framework an explicit signal that this is an internal route transition.

content.title: Navigation should describe intent
content.text:
Compare:

```tsx
<Link href="/products">Browse products</Link>
```

with a click handler that manually changes location.

The first communicates:

**This UI represents navigation to another route.**

That is a valuable engineering habit:

**Use the abstraction that expresses the user's intent.**

content.title: Dynamic routes
content.text:
Suppose the route tree contains:

```text
app/
  products/
    [id]/
      page.tsx
```

A product with id `42` can be linked with:

```tsx
<Link href="/products/42">Open product</Link>
```

The route structure determines which page receives the request.

content.question: Which option communicates internal navigation most directly?

options.text: A random button that changes unrelated state
A text node with no interaction

feedback.correct: Correct answer: A. A `Link` with an internal href
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: A. A `Link` with an internal href

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: Good framework code often starts with a good semantic description of what the user is trying to do.
nextSteps: Create three internal navigation links for `/`, `/products`, and `/settings`. For each, explain what route the link expresses.

Complete the checkpoint and explain the mechanism in your own words. A wrong first prediction is expected; the mastery signal is whether you can explain the result and handle a changed case after feedback.
